title.en: A God Without a Name: Viracocha, Pachacamac, Vsapu
title.zh: 無名之神:維拉科查、帕查卡馬克與烏薩普

region.zh: 秘魯(象徵性標記:庫斯科)(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by José de Acosta, publ. Hakluyt Society trans. 1880

source.work: José de Acosta, The Natural and Moral History of the Indies, vol. 2 (Books 5-7), ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1880

summary.en: They commonly acknowledge a supreme Lord and Author of all things, which they of Peru called Viracocha, and gave him names of great excellence, as Pachacamac, or Pachayachachic, which is the Creator of heaven and earth, and Vsapu, which is admirable. Him they did worship as the chiefest of all, whom they did honour in beholding the heaven. It hath caused great admiration in me, Acosta writes, that although they had this knowledge, yet had they no proper name for God: if we shall seek into the Indian tongue for a word to answer to this name of God, as in Latin Deus, in Greek Theos, in Hebrew Ii, in Arabike Alla, we shall not find any in the Cuscan tongues; such as preach use our Spanish name Dios. Yet in truth they had some little knowledge, and therefore in Peru they made him a rich temple, which they called Pachacamac, which was the principal sanctuary of the realm; and as this word is as much as to say the Creator, yet in this temple they used their idolatries, worshipping the devil and figures. They likewise made sacrifices and offerings to Viracocha, which held the chief place amongst the worships which the Kings Yncas made. Hereof they called the Spaniards Viracochas, for that they hold opinion they are the sons of heaven, and divine.
summary.zh: 秘魯土人素來承認有一位至尊之主、萬有之源,稱之為「維拉科查」,並以種種美名尊之:「帕查卡馬克」或「帕查亞查奇」——天地之造主;「烏薩普」——無比神奇者。他們奉他為至高,仰觀上天而致敬。阿科斯塔嘆道:奇哉,他們雖有此認知,卻無「神」的專名——在拉丁語中神名Dous,希臘語Theos,希伯來語Ii,阿拉伯語Alla;但在庫斯科語中竟找不到相當之詞!傳教士只能以西班牙語Dios稱之。然他們確有些微認知,故在秘魯為他建了一座富麗的神廟,名「帕查卡馬克」,為全國之首聖;只是廟中行的是偶像崇拜,拜的是魔鬼與雕像。他們也向維拉科查獻祭供奉,列印加諸王崇拜之首。西班牙人被稱為「維拉科查」,正因土人相信他們是「天之子、屬神之人」。

sensitivity.note: Acosta's argument from Acts 17 ('to the unknown God') is the classic missionary reading of Andean supreme-being religion; marked religious as a doctrinal record.

title.en: Thunder as a Man with Sling and Mace: Chuquilla, Catuilla, Intiillapa
title.zh: 雷為持彈弓與權杖之人:楚基利亞、卡圖利亞、因蒂利亞帕

region.zh: 庫斯科與全秘魯(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by José de Acosta, publ. Hakluyt Society trans. 1880

source.work: José de Acosta, The Natural and Moral History of the Indies, vol. 2 (Books 5-7), ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1880

summary.en: Next to Viracocha, or their supreme God, that which most commonly they have and do adore amongst the Infidels is the Sunne; and after, those things which are most remarkable in the celestial or elemental nature, as the moon, stars, sea and land. The Huacas, or Oratories, which the Yncas Lords of Peru had in greatest reverence next to Viracocha and the sun, was the thunder, which they called by three divers names, Chuquilla, Catuilla, and Intiillapa, supposing it to be a man in heaven, with a sling and a mace, and that it is in his power to cause raine, haile, thunder, and all the rest that appertains to the region of the aire, where the clouds engender. It was a Huaca generall to all the Indians of Peru, offering unto him many sacrifices; and in Cuzco, which is the Court and Metropolitan city, they did sacrifice children unto him, as to the Sunne. They did worship these three, Viracocha, the Sunne, and Thunder, after another manner than all the rest, as Polo writes: they did put, as it were, a gauntlet or glove upon their hands when they did lift them up to worship them. They did worship the earth, which they called Pachamama, as the Ancients did the goddess Tellus; and the sea likewise, which they call Mamacocha. Moreover they did worship the raine-bow, which were the arms and blazons of the Ynca, with two snakes stretched out on either side.
summary.zh: 繼維拉科查——他們的至尊之神——之後,秘魯土人最常拜的是太陽;其後則為天象與元素中最顯著者:月、星辰、海、大地。印加諸王崇敬次於維拉科查與太陽的瓦卡(聖所),便是雷霆——以三個名字稱之:楚基利亞、卡圖利亞、因蒂利亞帕。他們想象雷是一位身居天上的男子,手持彈弓與權杖;雨、雹、雷鳴,以及雲氣滋生的天空諸象,皆操於其手。此瓦卡為全秘魯印第安人所共奉,祭祀甚多;在都城庫斯科,人們像獻給太陽一樣,向他獻祭孩童。據波羅所述,他們拜維拉科查、太陽與雷時,別有一種禮節:舉手崇拜之際,手上要戴上如手套之物。他們拜大地「帕查瑪瑪」,如古人拜忒路斯;拜海洋「瑪瑪科查」。他們還拜彩虹——印加王的軍徽,兩側各伸出一條蛇。

sensitivity.note: Acosta's taxonomy of Peruvian cult (Polo's data); the gauntlet-worship detail is unique to this source.

title.en: The Shepherd's Star and the Jaguar in Heaven: Astral Patrons of Beasts
title.zh: 牧人星與天上的美洲豹:畜群星辰守護者

region.en: Shepherd country of the Collao (symbolic pin)
region.zh: 科利亞奧牧區(象徵性標記)

texts.period: Written by José de Acosta, publ. Hakluyt Society trans. 1880

source.work: José de Acosta, The Natural and Moral History of the Indies, vol. 2 (Books 5-7), ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1880

summary.en: Amongst the stars they all did commonly worship that which they called Colca, and we here the little goats (the Pleiades). They did attribute divers offices to divers stars, and those which had need of their favour did worship them: as the shepherd did sacrifice to a star which they called vrcuchillay, which they hold to be a sheep of divers colours, having the care to preserve their cattle. It is understood to be that which the Astronomers call Lyra. These shepherds worship two other stars which walk near unto them: they call them Catuchillay and vrcuchillay, and they fain them to be an ewe and a lambe. Others worshipped a star which they called Machachuay, to which they attribute the charge and power over serpents and snakes, to keep them from hurting of them. They ascribe power to another star which they called Chuquinchincay (which is as much as jaguar), over tigers, bears, and lions; and they have generally believed that of all the beasts of the earth there is one alone in heaven like unto them, the which hath care of their procreation and increase. And so they did observe and worship divers stars, as those which they called Chacana, Topatorca, Alcimana, Mirco, Miquiquiray, and many others.
summary.zh: 星辰之中,人人共拜的便是他們稱為「科爾卡」的那顆——即我們所說的小山羊(昴星團)。他們把不同的職司派給不同的星:凡有求於某星者便拜某星。牧人向名為「烏爾庫奇利亞」的星獻祭——相傳那是一頭斑斕彩色的羊,專司保佑畜群;天文學家說那便是天琴座。牧人還拜在它近旁行走的兩顆星:卡圖奇利亞與烏爾庫奇利亞,把它們想象為一只母羊與一只羊羔。另有人拜名為「馬查丘艾」的星,派它掌管蛇蟲,不許它們傷人。還有一星名為「楚基欽卡伊」(意即美洲豹),掌虎、熊、獅之力;他們普遍相信:世上所有走獸,天上各有一位同類照管其繁衍增殖。此外他們還觀測、崇拜「查卡納」「托帕托爾卡」「阿爾西馬納」「米爾科」「米基基拉伊」等許多星辰。

sensitivity.note: The astral-patron system: Acosta's list of dark-cloud constellations is the earliest attestation; jaguar-star tagged with world-serpent for the beast-in-heaven topos.

title.en: Acllahuasi, the House of the Chosen: Virgins for Gods, Sacrifices and the Inca
title.zh: 阿克利亞瓦西「選者之屋」:侍神、獻祭與王之側室

region.en: Monasteries of virgins, one in every province of Peru (symbolic pin: Cuzco)
region.zh: 秘魯各省貞女院(象徵性標記:庫斯科)

texts.period: Written by José de Acosta, publ. Hakluyt Society trans. 1880

source.work: José de Acosta, The Natural and Moral History of the Indies, vol. 2 (Books 5-7), ed. Sir Clements Markham, Hakluyt Society, 1880

summary.en: There were in Peru many monasteries of Virgins (for there are no other admitted), at the least one in every Province. In these monasteries there were two sorts of women: one ancient, which they called Mamaconas, for the instruction of the young; and the other of young maidens, placed there for a certain time, and after they were drawn forth, either for their gods or for the Ynca. They called this house or monastery Acllahuasi, which is to say, the house of the chosen. Every monastery had his Vicar or Governour called Appopanaca, who had liberty and power to choose whom he pleased, of what quality soever, being under eight years of age, if they seemed to be of a good stature and constitution. These Virgins thus shut up were instructed by the Mamaconas in diverse things needeful for the life of man, and in the customs and ceremonies of their gods; and afterwards they took them from thence, being above fourteen, sending them to the Court, whereof some were appointed to serve the Guacas and Sanctuaries, keeping their virginities for ever; some others were for the ordinary sacrifices that were made of maidens, and other extraordinary sacrifices, they made for the health, death, or wars of the Ynca; and the rest served for wives and concubines to the Ynca, and unto other his kinsfolkes and captaines, unto whom he gave them, which was a great and honourable recompence: this distribution was used every year. Those monasteries possessed rents and revenues for the maintenance of these Virgins. It was not lawful for any father to refuse his daughters when the Appopanaca required them for the service of these monasteries; yea, many fathers did willingly offer their daughters, supposing it was a great merit to be sacrificed for the Ynca. If any of these Mamaconas or Acllas were found to have trespassed against their honour, it was an inevitable chastisement to bury them alive, or to put them to death by some other kind of cruel torment.
summary.zh: 秘魯各地——至少每省一所——廣設貞女院(院中只收女子)。院內女眾分兩類:一類是年長者,稱「瑪瑪庫納」,司教導幼女之職;一類是少女,入院有定期,期滿之後或獻於諸神,或獻於印加王。此院名「阿克利亞瓦西」,意即「選者之屋」。每院設院長一名,稱「阿波帕納卡」,有權自行選取八歲以下、體格健美的女子入院。入院後由瑪瑪庫納教以人生所需諸藝,並學習諸神的習俗禮儀;十四歲以上便被送往王庭:其中一部分奉派侍奉瓦卡與聖所,終身守貞;一部分備作尋常與非常之處女獻祭——為印加王的健康、喪亡或征戰而設;其餘則為印加王及其親族、將領的妻妾,由王分賜之——這是一種崇高榮寵的報償。此種分配,年年舉行。貞女院的開支由專項收入維持。阿波帕納卡索人之時,為父者不得拒絕其女入院;許多父親竟欣然獻女,以為「為印加王獻身乃大功德」。瑪瑪庫納或阿克利亞若犯失貞之罪,懲罰絕無可免:活埋,或以其他酷刑處死。

sensitivity.note: The Aclla institution in Acosta's terse administrative account; flagged as a system involving child selection and capital punishment - recorded as archival evidence.
